title: Table, pictograph or bar graph: which one fits the job?
description: The same sweet choices of one class are shown three ways: a table with exact counts, a pictograph with one symbol for each child, and a bar graph with a bar for each sweet. Each display does one job best. Keeko doubts this and says a bar graph is best for everything.
teaching_notes: One idea: a table gives exact numbers, a pictograph gives a picture, and a bar graph lets us compare quickly, so we choose by the job. Watch for students who think one display is best for all data.

source: Table, pictograph or bar graph: which one to use
video_script.why: The child sees the same sweet data as a table, a pictograph and a bar graph, and learns which job each display does best.
video_script.substitution: The sweet choices of the book are shown in each of the three displays.
video_script.anchor: the sweet preferences of the students of the teacher in the book, shown as a table, a pictograph and a bar graph
video_script.wrong_answer: a bar graph is best for everything
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says a bar graph is best for everything, so a table is never needed. The bar graph was drawn from the numbers of the table, and the exact counts needed to buy the sweets come from the table, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Use a table for exact numbers, a pictograph for a picture, and a bar graph to compare fast

final_answer.value: table: exact numbers; pictograph: a picture; bar graph: compare fast
final_answer.spoken: a table gives exact numbers, a pictograph gives a picture, and a bar graph helps us compare fast

names.Ruhee: the teacher who asks the class for their favourite sweet

never_show: a bar graph is best for everything
maths_rules: children who chose: jalebi 6, gulab jamun 9, gujiya 13, barfi 3, rasgulla 7
table: every exact number is kept, one row for each sweet
pictograph: key 1 symbol = 1 child, so the rows have 6, 9, 13, 3 and 7 symbols
bar graph: scale 1 unit length = 1 child, so the bars are 6, 9, 13, 3 and 7 units tall, the bars start from 0
the tallest bar is gujiya with 13 units
slip: a bar graph is not best for everything, the exact counts to buy the sweets come from the table
video_script.design: The sweet counts of the book are drawn in three ways, one after the other, and each display gets its own job. The same sweets stay on the board all video.

<bookmark mark='three'/>The answers can be shown as a table, a pictograph or a bar graph.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which one shows the sweet most children like, at a glance?
